learning_outcomes.text: Identify, operate and calculate with the basic magnitudes of circuit theory and electrical machines, and apply mathematical analysis methods to the transient regime of circuits.
Analyze and solve problems with the transformer (transient, permanent, under load, no-load, tests, parameters, efficiency, couplings, as well as maneuver, tests and operation).
Apply and calculate the method for measuring active and reactive power for each specific case.
Solve unbalanced three-phase systems using symmetrical components.
Solve circuits by analyzing two-port networks.
Properly handle instrumentation and laboratory material necessary to perform tests and load transformers.
Know simulation programs that allow analyzing the operation of transformers under different operating situations.

syllabus_topics: Extension of Circuit Theory: magnetic coupling, steady-state analysis of the transformer, transient regime, two-port networks, power, three-phase circuits, electrometry.
Active and reactive power in balanced and unbalanced three-phase systems.
Measurement of active and reactive power in balanced and unbalanced three-phase systems.
Methods for measuring active and reactive power with single-phase wattmeters. Balanced and unbalanced systems. 4-wire and 3-wire systems.
Measurement of electrical parameters using a network analyzer.
Analysis of transient regime using the Laplace Transform method.
Inverse transform. Algebraic methods of decomposition into simple fractions. Table of transforms.
Circuit analysis in the 's' variable domain of Laplace.
Degree of unbalance and asymmetry of an unbalanced three-phase system.
Insertion of a two-port network into a circuit.
teaching_methods: Problem-solving classes, seminars, or practical cases

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam or partial cumulative/eliminatory exams
Utilization of practical activities (classroom, laboratory, computer lab, field, visits, etc.)
Resolution and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: There are two assessment modalities. For students choosing continuous evaluation (Modality 1), the final course grade is based on an 80% theoretical/practical exam, 10% utilization of practical activities, and 10% submitted assignments. The theoretical/practical exam itself is calculated as 0.4 times the theory test (ET) plus 0.6 times the problems test (EP); a grade below 5 in either ET or EP, or a 'NO APTO' in the essential practical test (EPR), results in a maximum final course grade of 4. For students choosing the global exam (Modality 2), the final grade is 0.8 times the theory exam (ETeo) plus 0.2 times the practical exam (EPrct); a grade of 4 or below in ETeo, or below 5 in EPrct, results in a maximum final course grade of 4. Practical activity grades are retained for resit examinations; if a student does not have a 'APTO' in practices, a practical exam must be taken during the resit.
